analysis.title: Gold's $4,000 Moment: The Cracks Are Starting To Show
key_insights: Gold is trapped between the $4,000 level and a major downward-sloping trendline. Today's candle is shaping up as the biggest downside move since the latest squeeze higher, and the bounce did not test the 50-day MA.
The report says compression is building and the eventual breakout could be violent.
Gold momentum is poor and a spike in yields adds pressure through a higher opportunity cost of holding a non-yielding asset. Unless yields reverse, the path of least resistance may stay lower.
The inverse gold/DXY relationship remains intact. With the dollar strengthening, the report calls aggressive gold bullishness without a weaker dollar a dangerous trade.
India's gold demand fell 29% YoY in Q3 while spending rose 3%, per the World Gold Council. Domestic prices were up 45%, so buyers paid more for less gold.
The share of Indian consumers expecting higher gold prices over the next three months fell from 69% to 61%. Investment-led jewellery buying slipped from 19% to 15%.

RBI gold purchases fell from 50 tonnes to 4 tonnes to 0.3 tonnes over the first nine months of 2024, 2025 and 2026. Gold's share of foreign reserves fell from 19% in January to 14.5% at the end of Q3.
Bar and coin demand fell 40% YoY in Q3.
The $4,000 level is the key battleground. A decisive break below it could turn the current compression into a much more painful move for bulls.
